findings.summary: The new periodic topology observer has no concrete bound or isolation from the authoritative metadata queue.
findings.evidence: 62/design.md:79-84 schedules engine-wide ListNodes every 5 s and retains labels after failed/oversized replies, but states no outstanding-request cap, aggregate cache/label byte bound, cancellation/deadline rule or scheduling isolation. Current flaminio-metaclient/src/lib.rs:98-120 uses an unbounded FIFO serviced by one serial worker; call_any at :124-145 tries each endpoint with the full timeout. flaminio-io/src/node.rs:308-314 sets that timeout to 3 s per endpoint. A three-endpoint stalled refresh can therefore occupy that worker for 9 s while more 5 s observations and existing heartbeat/membership work queue. Node-controlled labels are merged without a length bound at meta/service/service.go:197-205; the 1024-row/4MiB limits in 62/design.md:106-107 apply only to a report, not the new cache or pending refreshes.
findings.fix: Specify a bounded observer control path: at most one outstanding refresh, skipped/coalesced ticks while pending, exact node/zone/total-cache byte caps with atomic last-good-snapshot installation, a bounded timeout/backoff and generation/cancellation handling. Isolate or schedule observation work so it cannot build a backlog ahead of registration, membership and existing authoritative refresh work. Test stalled endpoints, repeated ticks, hostile/oversized labels, stale completions and continued bounded authoritative control progress; keep all metadata work off foreground I/O.

findings.summary: The report is built against a removed #47 control-socket contract and omits the current telemetry trust/resource boundary.
findings.evidence: 62/spec.md:S7 and design.md:18,91-109 require root stats [VOLUME] with a shared #47 stats-v1 object, latency fields and up to 4MiB/1024 rows. Actual reviewed 47/design.md:167-218 explicitly has no stats line: observations use #71 observe, schema 2, one pending snapshot, at most one snapshot/s, a 2 s engine wait and a 64KiB line; it explicitly identifies #62 as needing composition. 71/spec.md:S3 and contracts.md:40-87 reserve observations for that separate socket, define telemetry-off/privsep refusal and strict schema/unknown-key decoding. Current control.rs:55-60 spawns one thread per control connection; an individual reply-size bound does not bound repeated expensive snapshot requests. There is consequently no shared current producer/consumer contract or preserved scheduling boundary for the proposed traffic report.
findings.fix: Make #62 own a concrete whoever-lands-second extension of the current #71/#47 observation contract: exact request/schema/traffic fields, latency mapping, size/row refusal or another explicitly bounded exact mechanism, cache/rate/pending/time limits, telemetry-off and privsep behavior, upgrade order and Rust/Go golden/invalid fixtures. Preserve no truncation and the settled measurement semantics. Do not claim an existing #47 stats-v1 ABI or silently reopen/edit the clear dependency plans.

findings.summary: The declared network attribution tuple does not distinguish two target instances at the same epoch.
findings.evidence: 62/design.md:47-51 specifies immutable target-volume/epoch/peer attribution and requires dropping ended target generations, but gives no per-target-instance identity. That is insufficient in the standalone current source: Engine::handle(Input::Attach) at engine.rs:640-682 fetches GetVolume without allocating an epoch, detach at :1856 removes the runtime, and start_target at :1596-1621 accepts a token matching that same metadata epoch. Reattaching after detach can therefore construct another TargetRt with the same volume/epoch while an old decoded NetEvent is queued. The new direct late-session attribution intentionally bypasses the removed-key lookup, so volume/epoch alone can charge that old receipt to the replacement. ClientByteCounters at design.md:61-67 correctly use a distinct owned object, but the network path lacks an equivalent specified check.
findings.fix: Capture an immutable opaque target-instance generation (or an equivalent unique lifetime discriminator) when the runtime is constructed and carry it through outgoing sessions/events. Compare it with the current runtime before either flow lookup or any counter addition; old sessions of the same live generation may count Other, ended generations must add nothing. Add a detach/reattach test holding the same volume and metadata epoch constant with queued old replies. This is observation isolation, not a reason to change attach/fencing authority.

findings.summary: The later baseline assumes VM storage admission that the current clock contract explicitly refuses.
findings.evidence: 62/design.md:119-135 requires an exclusive fl-a/fl-b/fl-c VM run and presents it as the future authorized baseline without a #83 compatibility/refusal branch. Current reviewed 83/spec.md:S1 requires qualified physical Linux hosts and refuses virtualization/unknown provenance; 83/design.md:21-42 requires the attested clock contract before opening storage/registering/listening, provides no force bypass, and explicitly says the existing lab VMs are unqualified. This is an implementation-order/runtime compatibility constraint, not authorization that a later generic lab approval can override.
findings.fix: Specify the check preflight and result when #83 admission is active: refuse before mutating lab state on the current VMs, record the baseline as blocked/uncollected, and move the eventual workload to an explicitly qualified disposable physical topology or clearly identify a valid pre-#83 binary baseline and its limits. Add unsupported-profile fixture coverage. Never fabricate a physical-host attestation or weaken the clock profile for measurement.

findings.summary: Identity integration still points at #61/#72 and future v2 frames instead of the current #90 owner and composed profile.
findings.evidence: 62/spec.md:S4 and design.md:18-19,54-57,141 attribute ReplicaRef/routing contracts to #61/#72 and name future v2 frame tests. Current 61/design.md:8-22 is only a composition wrapper; 90/contracts.md:3-17 explicitly owns ReplicaRef and says #72 does not define it. 90/wire-contracts.md:3-22,65-89 defines exact ALPN flaminio-repl/4, HelloIdentity/FencedIdentity, captured ref/generation/session identity and active-profile sizes. Treating the old dependency description as the current hook leaves implementers testing the wrong composed codec and routing seam.
findings.fix: Point the measurement-only aggregation to #90 as the sole identity/wire owner, retain node-only aggregation without altering exact-ref authority, and specify whichever implementation lands second carries the immutable observer attribution through those routes and tests encoded lengths on the actual active ordinary/identity/snapshot/root profiles. Leave #61/#72/#90 unchanged and keep the historical #62 approval provenance separate from this correction.

report.scope: Full first-round security review of all four files under docs/issues/62 (intent, spec, design, decisions), cached actual issue body/comments, current affected Rust target/inflight, engine/network/codec/session, metaclient and ublk frontend paths, Go metadata authorization/labels/drain/control contracts, CSI topology and lab helper source. Read relevant current dependency contracts at the exact mapped HEADs above. No local appendices beyond those four files exist.
report.results: Five genuine comments: one High, three Medium, one Low; no additional Nits. The fixed-size per-inflight flow sidecar, no completed-operation history, local-network exclusion, checked counter overflow, attempted TX/decoded RX distinction, report-time unknown zones, strict frontend full-success offer hook, old client-counter-object isolation and no policy changes are appropriate in principle. Retained peer rows align with the pre-existing stable engine node vector; this review does not claim a new per-completed-operation history. Individual output refusal is specified, but is not an aggregate observer queue/cache bound. No new replication authority rule is proposed, so this measurement slice does not itself require a new safety mutant. The enabled/disabled observation equivalence and abuse tests remain future implementation work.
report.dependency_provenance: dependency_commits are actual checkout HEADs read, not approvals. In particular #90 technical clear commit is 331f337d3b847ff2d4faabc572f4ceae74837cd7 and its report HEAD is c9231b243dceb196a0eccb615055887c9879bb73; #61 is now composition only. Clear dependencies were inspected read-only. Historical 2026-11-13 approvals and settled engine-handoff/report-time-label boundaries are preserved; lack of new approval is not a finding.
